verdict.reasoning: Printed page 277 (PDF p301), 13.7.1: the Term/Subclause table has four aligned rows in one block (77-level-entry, constant-entry, record-description-entry, type-declaration-entry), with no break between rows 2 and 3. In page-301.md, only the first two rows are inside the pipe table; record-description-entry and type-declaration-entry follow a blank line as a loose paragraph joined by a backslash line break. Both sources are quoted accurately. The wording of every row is intact, so this does not change normative meaning. It is a genuine structural defect, though, not just wrapping: anything that parses the markdown table, whether a tool or a reader, gets two of the four term-to-subclause mappings. The severity is correctly 'structural', not 'normative'. The diagram above it (a bracket around four stacked alternatives, then an ellipsis) matches the PDF apart from the box-drawing rendering, and it is not part of this claim.
